mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.2%) signals accommodative monetary policy that compresses equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced cost of capital for corporate valuation.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >50% of periods with FEDFUNDS < 0.2%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 0.5% (FEDFUNDS > 0.5%) signals monetary tightening that elevates equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days through reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >50% of periods with FEDFUNDS > 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rises in FEDFUNDS (>0.1% increase) and CPIAUCSL (>0.1% increase) signal accelerating monetary tightening amid inflation, compressing equity valuations and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1% and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.1% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >50% of periods with both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rising >0.1% in 1 month, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 8.0%), a decline in unemployment rate (>0.1pp decrease) signals improving labor market conditions, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >50% of periods with UNRATE > 8.0% and UNRATE decline >0.1pp in 1 month, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong nonfarm payroll growth (PAYEMS > 0.5% annualized) indicates robust labor market expansion, supporting consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in >50% of periods with PAYEMS growth > 0.5% (annualized), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts above 750,000 units (HOUST > 750) signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, supporting retail sales and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >50% of periods with HOUST > 750, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST > 0.5% rise) and retail sales (RSAFS > 0.5% rise) signal accelerating consumer demand, driving corporate revenue growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 0.5% and RSAFS rises > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >50% of periods with both HOUST and RSAFS rising >0.5% in 1 month, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1 > 1.0% annualized) indicates robust economic expansion, supporting corporate earnings and investor confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in >50% of periods with GDPC1 growth > 1.0% (annualized), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
